newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain farmers fear crop damage after heavy rains.
newsitem.headline: Spain farmers fear crop damage after heavy rains.

text.p: This year's Spanish cereal crop may be reduced because of the difficulty of entering fields to sow winter wheat and barley after heavy rain, the farmers association ASAJA said on Friday.

"In the south particularly they're having great problems with the floods and they fear that they may lose a substantial amount of hectarage because they haven't been able to get in there and sow," a spokesman said.
He said he was unable to estimate at this early stage how much of the crop might be lost, and this would depend on how the weather fared into the spring.
Farmers were hoping the weather would dry up sufficiently to sow short-cycle wheat and barley, which requires less time to ripen, he said.
Although the rain had held off for a few days, it had not abated sufficiently for the land to dry out, experts said.
But the delayed maize crop in the central and northern parts of Spain should be relatively unscathed by the bad weather, a trader in Barcelona said.

"Maize has a strong stalk and unlike wheat and barley it doesn't bend when it rains, but manages to withstand. Although a good part of the crop has yet to be brought in, it shouldn't be too damaged," he said.

He estimated that around half of the maize crop in central Spain and about a third in northern regions had not been harvested yet, although it was difficult to estimate what quantity this might entail.
